rationale_samples: Hijack/hijacking benefits appear in benefit tables for Budget Direct, Insure&Go and Tick. The baseline has a hijack_kidnap_and_ransom category but lacks a comparable top-level limit.

proposed_update.name: hijack_or_hijacking_limit
proposed_update.description: Hijack, aircraft hijack, airline hijack or public-transport hijacking benefit limit as printed, including per-24-hour amounts and total cap if concise.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: International benefits table row '13* Hijacking' shows $5,000 for Comprehensive; Section 13 pays $1,000 for each 24-hour period detained, maximum $5,000.
Corporate benefits tables row 'Hijacking' shows $Nil / $10,000 / $30,000 / $30,000; Section 13 pays $1,000 per continuous 24-hour period.
Cruise benefits table row I 'Airline hijack' shows Nil / Nil / $2,500; Section I covers aircraft or sea vessel hijacked for more than 24 hours.

rationale_samples: Hijacking/aircraft hijack is a recurring headline benefit in benefits tables and is not currently available as a major flat limit despite an existing taxonomy category.

proposed_update.name: hijacking_limit
proposed_update.description: Hijacking, aircraft hijack or public-transport hijack detention benefit limit as printed, including per-24-hour payment and maximum where concise.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Corporate benefits tables row 'Identity theft protection' shows $Nil / $10,000 / $15,000 / $15,000. Section 19 reimburses legal expenses to close disputed accounts, rectify records and defend creditor actions after stolen documents cause identity theft.

rationale_samples: Identity theft protection is a named corporate travel benefit with a specific limit and legal/remediation scope; current schema has travel_documents_limit but not identity restoration expenses.

proposed_update.name: identity_theft_protection_limit
proposed_update.description: Identity theft protection limit as printed, including legal expenses, document replacement, credit-rating restoration or account rectification expenses arising from stolen personal data/documents.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p9-t1 Inbound Plan Section 19: Emergency Dental Expenses in Australia $2,000; p41-t1: Emergency Dental Expenses in Australia $2,000.
p69 Benefit 21 describes Dental expenses: emergency dental treatment provided in Australia by a qualified dentist to relieve pain or temporarily restore function.

rationale_samples: Inbound PDS wording often separates emergency dental treatment in Australia from inbound medical expenses and from overseas dental limits. A distinct field improves comparison with inbound medical cover.

proposed_update.name: inbound_emergency_dental_in_australia_limit
proposed_update.description: Emergency dental expenses limit for non-Australian residents travelling to Australia where treatment is provided in Australia, as printed, e.g. $2,000, $1,000, Nil. Use only for inbound-specific dental expenses in Australia.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Corporate benefits tables row 'Kidnap and ransom' shows $100,000 / $250,000 / $500,000 / $500,000; Section 12 lists reimbursed ransom monies, negotiator fees, reward, loan costs, travel/accommodation and salary costs.

rationale_samples: Kidnap and ransom appears as a high-value business travel benefit distinct from hijacking. It is business-specific but important for comparing corporate travel insurance.

proposed_update.name: kidnap_ransom_limit
proposed_update.description: Kidnap and ransom benefit limit as printed, including reimbursement for ransom monies, negotiator costs, related travel/accommodation, salaries or other kidnap/extortion costs where covered.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Page 15 requires reporting loss/theft to police or responsible transport provider and obtaining a written report within 72 hours of discovering the loss/theft or as soon as reasonably practicable.
Page 46 requires reporting loss/theft of luggage, personal effects, travel documents or money to police, transport provider or accommodation provider within 7 days of first becoming aware.
Pages 27-28 say Allianz expects loss/theft to be reported to police or transport authority where reasonably practicable and may reduce claims for unreasonable delay or failure.

rationale_samples: Loss/theft reporting deadlines and responsible authorities are frequent baggage/document/cash claim conditions. Because some PDSs use hours, days or 'as soon as practicable', a string field is safer than a single numeric days field.

proposed_update.name: loss_theft_report_deadline
proposed_update.description: Deadline and authority requirements for reporting lost, stolen or damaged luggage, money, travel documents, phones or valuables, preserving wording such as 24 hours, 72 hours, 7 days, as soon as practicable, police, carrier, hotel/security or issuing bank.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Section 5 Delayed Luggage Allowance: 'If all Your luggage is delayed ... for more than 12 hours'.
Benefits tables and Section 9: Essentials/Essentials Plus after 12 hours; Ultimate/Ultimate Plus after 8 hours.
Section E3 Delayed baggage covers baggage delayed by airline or transport company 'for more than 8 hours'.
Section D2 Delayed baggage covers baggage delayed 'for more than 24 hours'.
Section D.4.3 covers checked-in baggage delayed 'for more than 12 hours from the time you arrive at your destination'.

rationale_samples: Baggage delay thresholds differ materially across insurers and tiers. The baseline captures the limit but not the waiting trigger as a stable comparable field.

proposed_update.name: luggage_delay_minimum_delay_hours
proposed_update.description: Minimum checked baggage/luggage delay in hours before delayed baggage or luggage delay benefit can be claimed for this plan/record. If thresholds differ by tier or sub-benefit, record the applicable value for the emitted plan and preserve details in coverage_benefits/sub_limits.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p66: Delay of Luggage and Personal Effects applies where items are delayed, misdirected or misplaced by the Carrier for more than 12 hours.
p38: Delayed baggage benefit applies if baggage is delayed by an airline or transport company for more than 8 hours.
p28: luggage delayed, misdirected or misplaced by carrier for more than 10 consecutive hours.
p35-p36: delayed baggage and baggage delay before boarding benefits apply for delays of more than 24 hours.

rationale_samples: Delayed baggage waiting periods differ materially and are prominent in benefit wording/tables. Current luggage_delay_limit does not separately normalise the trigger threshold.

proposed_update.name: luggage_delay_waiting_period_hours
proposed_update.description: Initial delay threshold in hours before delayed luggage/baggage benefit becomes payable where a single threshold applies. If thresholds vary by journey leg, plan or before-boarding/on-trip benefit, capture details in coverage_benefits or sub_limits.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p13: Frequent Traveller Saver lets customers choose 15, 25, 40 or 63 days for each trip.
p9: multiple trips up to selected maximum duration 30, 45 or 60 days for International policies; Bare Essentials no trips longer than 30 days and Silver no longer than 45 days.
p4-t1: Maximum trip duration varies by age and destination, including 42 days, 90 days and 365 days.

rationale_samples: Selectable maximum trip duration options are not limited to annual/multi-trip policies. Cruise and single-trip products also show maximum duration choices that vary by age, destination and tier. This is an explicit applies_to/description broadening for review.

proposed_update.description: Available maximum duration options for a journey/trip, expressed as a readable string when multiple options exist, e.g. 15/30/45 days, 30/45/60 days, 42/90/365 days by age or destination. Use for annual multi-trip per-journey duration choices and for single-trip/cruise products where the PDS states selectable or plan-dependent maximum trip durations. If a single value applies to the extracted record, use maximum_trip_duration_days instead.
proposed_update.name: maximum_trip_duration_options

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Page 41 states if admitted to hospital or outpatient treatment is likely to exceed $2,000, the traveller should contact Allianz Global Assistance to seek approval.
Pages 5 and 35 state prior approval is required if admitted to hospital, need surgery, or expect medical and related expenses over $2,000.
Page 35 states the emergency assistance team should be phoned as soon as possible if hospitalisation is required, medical expenses will exceed $2,000, or early return is wanted.
Page 64 states if hospitalised or outpatient treatment total cost will exceed $1,000, assistance service prior approval is required.

rationale_samples: Many PDSs specify a monetary threshold above which emergency assistance/prior approval must be contacted for medical, hospital or evacuation costs. The baseline emergency_assistance_details can hold this in text, but a numeric AUD field improves stable comparison and compliance extraction.

proposed_update.name: medical_assistance_approval_threshold_aud
proposed_update.description: AUD threshold above which the insured must contact emergency assistance or obtain prior approval for medical, hospital, outpatient, surgery, evacuation or similar expenses, where a single dominant threshold is stated.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p3/p4 footnote: Cover will not exceed 12 months from onset of the illness, condition or injury; p29 says cover applies for a maximum of 12 months from date of suffering.
p64: medical or hospital expenses incurred within 12 months after an illness first showed itself or the injury happened.
p7 footnote: Medical and dental cover and assistance will not exceed 12 months from onset of illness or injury; p51 repeats maximum of 12 months.
p32 exclusion: expenses incurred more than 12 months from the time you first received treatment for the injury or illness.

rationale_samples: Several PDSs cap medical, dental, evacuation or COVID medical cover to expenses incurred within 12 months from onset/treatment. This is a stable eligibility/benefit-duration constraint that is hard to compare if embedded only in notes.

proposed_update.name: medical_expenses_continuation_limit_months
proposed_update.description: Maximum period in months after onset of illness, injury or condition during which emergency medical, dental, evacuation, repatriation or related expenses remain payable, where stated as a general medical benefit duration cap.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: International benefits table and Section 1 note: 'Cover will not exceed 12 months from onset of the illness, condition or injury'.
Benefits tables footnote: 'Cover will not exceed 18 months from onset of the illness, condition or injury'; Section 1 repeats maximum 18 months.
Section B1 exclusion 8: no cover for expenses incurred more than 12 months from the time first treatment was received for injury or illness.

rationale_samples: Overseas medical cover often has a maximum period from illness/injury onset even when the dollar limit is unlimited. This materially affects comparison and is not captured by emergency_medical_limit.

proposed_update.name: medical_expenses_max_months_from_onset
proposed_update.description: Maximum number of months emergency medical/dental expenses cover may continue from onset of illness, condition or injury, where stated separately from the policy/trip duration.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Page 21 states Allianz will pay for treatment received and/or hospital accommodation up to a maximum period of 12 months after the sickness first presented or injury occurred.

Page 51 says medical/dental cover applies for a maximum of 12 months from the date of suffering the disabling injury, sickness or disease; p69 repeats this for inbound Australian medical/dental expenses.
Page 64 states medical or hospital expenses must be incurred within 12 months after an illness first showed itself or the injury happened; p94 repeats this for onboard cruise medical expenses.

rationale_samples: Several PDSs impose a maximum period for ongoing medical/dental treatment after the onset of illness or injury, commonly 12 months. This is a structured medical-cover condition not captured by emergency_medical_limit.

proposed_update.name: medical_treatment_maximum_period_months
proposed_update.description: Maximum period in months for which covered medical, hospital, dental, evacuation or related treatment expenses may be payable from onset of the illness/injury, where stated.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p4 and p5 benefits tables list Missed Connections: International Comprehensive $3,000, Domestic $2,000; p40 Section 10 sets conditions and limits.
p15 Australian Travel Plan schedule: Missed connection - special events $2,000; Missed connection – flight delay within Australia $2,000; p32-p33 details both benefits.

rationale_samples: Missed connection cover is a separate benefit in Budget Direct and nib domestic plans, and is not cleanly represented by travel_delay or special_events alone.

proposed_update.name: missed_connections_limit
proposed_update.description: Missed connection benefit limit as printed, including general missed connections, missed flight connections, missed cruise/tour connections and special-event missed connection variants where separately stated.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p55: Version IG_AMT_PDS_0426_02.
p2: Prepared on 19 December 2025; POL849 / IMP3748.
p2: TK_EAA_PW_CRS_0426.

rationale_samples: Several documents contain non-date version or document identifiers useful for traceability. The baseline has dates and source hash/path but no field for the printed PDS/version code.

proposed_update.name: pds_version_identifier
proposed_update.description: Printed PDS version code, product code, document reference or form identifier where stated, excluding dates already captured in pds_effective_date or pds_prepared_or_version_date.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p5 domestic benefits table: Cover for self-drive holidays in Australia - Personal vehicle insurance excess $2,500; p38 Domestic Plan bonus cover reimburses up to $2,500 for personal car or motorcycle comprehensive policy excess or repair costs.

rationale_samples: Own/personal vehicle insurance excess appears as a domestic self-drive benefit in Budget Direct, but has limited support in the supplied corpus. Candidate should be reviewed before adding as a stable schema field.
reject_rationale_samples: Commbank's Domestic Plan bonus for excess on the traveller's own personal vehicle is unusual and closer to a domestic motor-vehicle add-on than a standard travel-insurance comparison field. It should be captured in coverage_benefits or optional_add_ons if present, not promoted to a reusable top-level field.

proposed_update.name: personal_vehicle_excess_limit
proposed_update.description: Domestic self-drive personal vehicle insurance excess benefit limit as printed, where the policy reimburses excess or repair costs for the traveller’s own car or motorcycle rather than a rental vehicle.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Domestic benefits table row 'Cover for self-drive holidays in Australia - Personal vehicle insurance excess' shows $2,500; Section 7 Domestic Plan bonus cover reimburses up to $2,500 for excess or repair costs on personal car or motorcycle.

Corporate Ultimate extras table includes 'Personal car excess &/or repairs' $2,000 and 'Personal car loss of no claim bonus and/or $500 per week for a hire car' $2,500; Sections 27 and 28 detail these covers.

rationale_samples: Personal car/self-drive vehicle excess benefits appear in domestic and business products and are distinct from rental vehicle excess. The baseline rental_vehicle_excess_limit should not be overloaded for a traveller’s own vehicle.

proposed_update.name: personal_vehicle_excess_or_repair_limit
proposed_update.description: Personal vehicle, self-drive holiday car/motorcycle excess, personal car repairs, no-claim-bonus or hire-car reimbursement limit as printed, where cover applies to the insured person's own vehicle rather than a rental vehicle.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p10 and p54: D.3.4 Pet services $100 each day up to $1,000 each person for extra daily costs of keeping pets in a registered boarding facility.
p5 international table: Pet care Nil/Nil/$600; p46 Section J covers extra kennel or cattery fees if final inward aircraft journey is delayed more than 24 hours.
p15 benefits table: Pet care Nil/Nil/Nil/$600; p40 Section J covers extra kennel or cattery fees for delayed final inward journey.

p41 Coronavirus travel costs includes reasonable additional pet care services, including kennel/cattery boarding fees or professional pet sitting services in Australia, subject to the Coronavirus travel costs limit.

rationale_samples: Pet care/services benefits are separately listed in SCTI, Insure&Go and Tick and often have their own sublimits rather than being part of general additional expenses.

proposed_update.name: pet_care_limit
proposed_update.description: Pet care, pet services, kennel, cattery, boarding or professional pet sitting benefit limit as printed, including daily amount and total cap if concise.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Cruise benefits table row J 'Pet care' shows Nil / Nil / $600; Section J covers extra kennel or cattery fees if final inward aircraft journey is delayed more than 24 hours.
Benefits table and Sections D.3.4-D.3.5 show Pet services and Childcare expenses: '$100 for each day $1,000 for each person'.

rationale_samples: Pet boarding/kennel and childcare/domestic services benefits are in the taxonomy but lack flat fields. They are recurring enough to compare when offered, while details can remain in coverage_benefits.

proposed_update.name: pets_childcare_domestic_services_limit
proposed_update.description: Pet boarding, kennel/cattery, pet services, childcare or domestic services benefit limit as printed, including daily amount and maximum where concise.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p12: extension can be applied for before expiry; free extension for unforeseeable circumstances until able to travel home or six months; combined period cannot exceed 24 months.
p20: necessary extension due to unforeseeable circumstances extends cover for up to 12 months or until able to travel home; voluntary extension requires contact before end date.

p14 and p48: extending journey requires purchase of a new policy before expiry; free extension where journey necessarily extended due to unforeseeable circumstance until physically able to travel home.

rationale_samples: Policy extension terms recur across insurers and affect duration/eligibility but are not explicitly represented except indirectly in refund terms or maximum duration fields.

proposed_update.name: policy_extension_terms
proposed_update.description: Rules for extending cover or automatic/free extension where a trip is necessarily extended, including whether voluntary extensions require a new policy, approval requirements, maximum extension duration, exclusions for already-travelling or annual policies, and contact requirements.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Page 8 states International plans provide up to 30,000EUR for overseas funeral expenses or repatriation of remains for Schengen; page 32 states funeral/cremation or returning remains to Australia maximum $20,000 or 30,000EUR in Schengen.
Section 4.2 states death expenses maximum $20,000, or 30,000EUR for Schengen Visa death in a Schengen member state.
Table of Benefits B1 and M2 rows state 'Return of body or ashes to Australia $50,000 or up to €30,000 for Schengen countries; Funeral or burial expenses outside Australia $10,000'.
Section D.1.5 'Funeral expenses or return of mortal remains' pays up to $50,000 to the estate of each deceased person.

rationale_samples: Repatriation/funeral remains cover is a core recurring medical-adjacent benefit with materially different sub-limits, including Schengen amounts, and deserves a stable comparison field separate from emergency_medical_limit.

proposed_update.name: repatriation_of_remains_limit
proposed_update.description: Funeral expenses, burial/cremation, return of body, ashes or mortal remains limit as printed, including Schengen visa EUR amounts and whether the limit is per person or per deceased person.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p32 Section 2 Additional Expenses: pays reasonable expenses incurred in returning a Rental Vehicle to the nearest depot if you are unfit to drive on written medical advice.
p7 domestic table: Return of rental car Nil/Nil/$750; p47: Domestic Gold reimburses up to $750 for return to nearest depot if doctor certifies unfit to drive.
p15 Australian Travel Plan schedule: Return of rental vehicle $750; p35: pays towards return to nearest depot including airport concession charges if unable to do so due to a claimable event.

rationale_samples: Return of a rental vehicle to a depot is a recurring ancillary rental-vehicle benefit with its own limit in Insure&Go and nib, and appears under additional expenses/rental vehicle wording in Budget Direct. It is distinct from reimbursement of rental vehicle excess.

proposed_update.name: return_rental_vehicle_limit
proposed_update.description: Return of rental vehicle, rental car or rental vehicle depot-return benefit limit as printed, including conditions such as medical unfitness to drive.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p30: Basic plan if valid Schengen Visa and death in a Schengen member state, pay up to 30,000EUR for expenses incurred in that Schengen member state.
p23-t1 and p67: In event of death in a Schengen member state, €30,000 EUR.
p53: if valid Schengen Visa and death in Schengen member state, maximum 30,000EUR for expenses incurred in that state.
p4-t1/p31: return of body or ashes to Australia $50,000 or up to €30,000 for Schengen countries; funeral or burial expenses outside Australia $10,000.

rationale_samples: Schengen visa repatriation amounts are repeatedly disclosed as a distinct sub-limit/alternative to the AUD repatriation limit. A dedicated field helps preserve foreign-currency requirements without overloading the main repatriation limit.

proposed_update.name: schengen_repatriation_limit
proposed_update.description: Schengen visa repatriation, funeral or return-of-remains limit as printed, including currency and conditions, e.g. €30,000 EUR if death occurs in a Schengen member state while holding a valid Schengen visa.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Comprehensive table p9-t1 and Multi-Trip table p11-t1 include '3.3 Alternative Transport Expenses' with $5,000 single/per person limits, and p26 describes transport to arrive on time for a wedding, funeral, pre-paid tour/cruise, conference, sporting event or concert/cultural event.
Tables p9-t1 and text p44/p53 list 'Delayed journey to a special event' up to $2,500 for each person before departure and on-trip.
Tables p7-t1, p59-t1 and p59-t2 list Benefit 9 'Special Events' ($5,000 Comprehensive; $2,000 Domestic) and Benefit 10 'Festivals and Gigs' ($2,000 or $5,000 depending plan).

Benefits table p25-t2 lists Section 17 'Special Event Transport Expenses' with $2,000 for Comprehensive/Overseas Frequent Traveller and Already Overseas; p88 covers weddings, funerals, conferences, concerts, music festivals, sporting events or tours over two nights.

rationale_samples: Special-event alternative transport is a recurring standalone benefit across the supplied PDSs, but the baseline only includes a taxonomy category and no top-level limit field. A stable string limit supports comparison while detailed rows remain in coverage_benefits.

proposed_update.name: special_events_limit
proposed_update.description: Special event or alternative transport benefit limit as printed, covering weddings, funerals, conferences, concerts/festivals/gigs, sporting events, tours or other time-critical events where the traveller needs alternative transport to arrive on time.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Page 8: 'A single item limit may be increased to $10,000 by paying an additional premium'; Section 8 optional cover says limit can be increased by up to $10,000 per single item.
Additional Specified Items Cover table: 'E2 Specified items $4,000 for a single item; Single article, Pair or Set limit up to $8,000 for combined items'.
Section D.4.2: specified item value can be '$1,500 to $10,000 for each item'; benefits table shows '$10,000 for each item' and '$15,000 for all items'.
Page 10 and benefits table footnote: item limits may be increased by paying additional premium, with specified receipt/valuation requirements.

rationale_samples: Optional specified/high-value item cover is common and highly comparable. Existing optional_add_ons can capture details, but a numeric maximum per item supports stable comparison.

proposed_update.name: specified_item_max_per_item_aud
proposed_update.description: Maximum additional or specified item limit per single item in AUD where the plan allows purchase of extra cover for specified luggage/personal effects items. Use sub_limits/optional_add_ons for aggregate specified item limits and eligibility proof requirements.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p12: Increase luggage item limit cover; p34 states multiple-item overall increase cannot exceed $15,000.
p40-p41 High Value Items: additional cover up to total $5,000; cannot be more than 12 months old except medical aids; excludes drones, jewellery, watches and watercraft.
p17 Increase Luggage Item Limits; p18 Electronic Gadgets cover up to maximum $5,000 with item limits.
p6-t2 Additional Specified Items Cover: $4,000 for a single item, up to $8,000 combined items; available on Silver and Gold.
p17-t3 Additional Specified Items Cover: $4,000 for a single item, up to $6,000 combined items; p34 states optional cover available on Top level.

rationale_samples: Most reviewed PDSs include an optional high-value/specified-item/increased luggage item-limit feature. It is important for luggage comparison and is better surfaced than burying only in optional_add_ons.

proposed_update.name: specified_items_or_high_value_items_cover_options
proposed_update.description: Options and limits for specified high-value items or increased luggage item limits, including availability by plan, per-item limit, combined total limit, excluded item types, receipt/valuation age requirements and whether an extra premium is required.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: Section 8 Travel Delay: 'pre-booked, prepaid transport is temporarily delayed ... for at least 6 hours' and pays up to $300 again for each full 24-hour period.
Section 5 Travel delay: pre-booked transport delayed 'for at least 6 hours'; benefits tables also say 'Includes up to $200 after 6 hours delay'.
Section D Travel delay expenses covers delays 'for more than 12 hours'; table shows $50 or $150 per completed 12 hours depending tier.
Section C Travel delay expenses covers final internal aircraft departure delayed 'for more than 12 hours'.

rationale_samples: Travel delay benefits are frequently compared by both dollar limit and delay threshold. The baseline has travel_delay_limit but no structured trigger threshold, causing important table data to be buried in text.

proposed_update.name: travel_delay_minimum_delay_hours
proposed_update.description: Minimum transport delay in hours before the travel delay benefit can be claimed for this plan/record. If thresholds differ by sub-benefit, use coverage_benefits or sub_limits for detail.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p68: Travel Delay reimburses after Carrier delay/rescheduled departure for at least 6 hours and subsequent full 24-hour periods.
p36: Travel delay expenses apply if an individual leg is delayed for more than 12 hours.
p26: Travel Delay Expenses apply after an unexpected delay of at least 6 consecutive hours.

rationale_samples: Travel delay threshold is a high-value comparison attribute and varies materially across insurers (6, 12, 24 hours). Current travel_delay_limit may preserve it only if manually included, and waiting_period_hours is too generic.

proposed_update.name: travel_delay_waiting_period_hours
proposed_update.description: Initial delay threshold in hours before the travel delay benefit becomes payable where a single threshold applies to the extracted record. If thresholds vary by plan, benefit or transport mode, capture details in coverage_benefits or sub_limits.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p3-t1 International benefits table Section 3 Travel Services Provider Insolvency: $Nil / $5,000 / $10,000; p31-t1 Domestic/International limits table for Section 3.
p109 General Exclusion 7: Financial collapse of any accommodation, tour, transport provider, booking agent, or travel agency is excluded.
p22 General Exclusion 27 excludes refusal/failure to provide services by reason of financial default; p57 defines financial default.

rationale_samples: Travel provider insolvency/financial default is handled inconsistently across insurers: some include a benefit, others exclude it. A dedicated limit/status field supports stable cross-insurer comparison beyond generic exclusions.

proposed_update.name: travel_services_provider_insolvency_limit
proposed_update.description: Travel services provider insolvency, financial default or financial collapse benefit limit/status as printed, e.g. $5,000, $10,000, Nil, excluded/not covered. Capture whether travel agent/tour operator insolvency is excluded in notes or coverage_benefits.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p9 Policy types: Individual, Couple, Family; definitions describe one adult plus dependants, two adults in partner relationship, or two adults plus accompanying dependent children.
p3 Policy Types: Individual, Couple, Family; p14 table applies to individual, couple and family cover.
p9-t1 Non-medical Single Trip - One adult per policy; p42 defines you/yourself and accompanied children, and notes Domestic Plan applies per person only.

rationale_samples: Some insurers sell or disclose party-cover options such as Individual, Couple and Family, with implications for dependent children and per-policy limits. It is somewhat less universal than benefit limits but useful for product-configuration extraction.

proposed_update.name: traveller_party_options
proposed_update.description: Available insured-party or policyholder group options for the product, e.g. Individual, Couple, Family, one adult per policy, family cover. Include dependency/supervision rules only if not captured in dependent_child_age_limit_years or eligibility_rules.

evidence_documents.quote_or_summary: p13: Snow Sports Plus Policy includes cover; p27 says if you do not purchase the Snow Sports Plus Policy and participate in listed snow sports you will not have cover.
p19: Snow Pack optional pack; must be aged under 75; benefits 7.8-7.13.
p6: Winter Sports Cover upgrade; no cover if upgrade not purchased.
p22: Snow Sports and Snow Sports+ are options to vary cover, not available on Cancellation Only or Non-Medical.

rationale_samples: Winter/snow sports cover is handled as a plan tier by some insurers and an add-on by others. A status field analogous to cruise_cover_status would improve stable comparison while detailed benefits remain in coverage_benefits/optional_add_ons.

proposed_update.name: winter_sports_cover_status
proposed_update.description: Winter sports or snow sports cover status for the plan: included, optional add-on, separate plan/tier, excluded, not applicable, or unknown. Use detailed benefit limits and activity rules in coverage_benefits, optional_activity_cover and optional_add_ons.
